resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
requirements: All utilities on for the inspection; lockbox code if vacant
Trash and debris cleared inside and out
Walkways level and free of trip hazards
4 inch contrasting house number visible from the street
Graspable handrail on steps with more than four risers; guardrails on open stairs
Windows and doors operable, no cracked or broken glass
No pest or rodent infestation
Egress window or door in every bedroom; no bedrooms in basements
Bathroom window or exhaust fan
Dryer vent hard piped to the outside
Water heater discharge pipe ending 2 to 6 inches above the floor
Smoke detectors working on every level, under 10 years old, 10-year sealed battery if battery powered, hardwired units interconnected and not swapped for battery units
CO detector within 10 feet of each bedroom
Pools, fences, garages and decks safe; pool gates self-closing and self-latching
Wood-burning fireplace or stove needs a certificate showing it is in good working order
Thumb-turn locks (no keyed interior locks)
All open permits closed with final inspections; unpermitted work must be documented before the CCO is issued

fees.label: Initial CCO inspection
fees.quote: **Initial inspection fee is $100 and a re-inspection fee of $50 in the event a re-inspection is required**

fees.label: Re-inspection
fees.quote: **Initial inspection fee is $100 and a re-inspection fee of $50 in the event a re-inspection is required**

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Inspection Application for Certificate of Continued Occupancy (check 'House Sale') and submit it to the Construction Department, 59 S. White Horse Pike, Berlin. The Tax Collector must certify that taxes are current and there are no liens. Inspection requests can be emailed to construction@berlinnj.org.

evidence.quote: INSPECTION APPLICATION FOR CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUED OCCUPANCY
**NOTE** ALL OPEN PERMITS MUST BE CLOSED WITH FINAL PASSING INSPECTIONS BEFORE A CCO CAN BE ISSUED.
RESOLUTION 2020 -078 - RESOLUTION OF THE BOROUGH OF BERLIN, COUNTY OF CAMDEN, STATE OF NEW JERSEY, AUTHORIZING REFUND OF RESALE INSPECTION FEE OF $100.

resale_co.notes: The Borough runs a resale CCO inspection (the application has a 'House Sale' checkbox and council reports list 'Resale Inspection Fees'), but no Borough page or ordinance text found states in plain words that a CCO is mandatory before every sale; the ordinance on ecode360 could not be opened. The same application is used for rentals and commercial properties. Lead time and validity are not published.

requirements: Battery smoke detectors must be 10-year sealed battery units (Bureau notice, 'Effective Immediately')
Hardwired smoke alarms from original construction may not be replaced with battery alarms
If the home has a monitored alarm system, notify the alarm company before the test and have the codes available at the inspection

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance and mail it with a check payable to 'Borough of Berlin' to Berlin Bureau of Fire Prevention, PO Box 226, Berlin, NJ 08009. The property must be ready for inspection.

evidence.quote: The application fee for a certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance (CSDCMAC), as required by N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3, shall be based upon the amount of time remaining before the change of occupant is expected, as follows:
Certificates are valid for (60) days from the date of the inspection.
All battery smoke detectors must be the 10-year sealed battery units.

evidence.doc_date: 2026-07 (LEA registry as of June 30, 2026); key: F = Fire Department

evidence.quote: Berlin Borough is the LEA for Waterford Township. AS OF APRIL2025 NO LONGER A SHARED SERVICE

fire_cert.notes: Certificates are valid for 60 days from the inspection. Questions line on the form: 856-767-6839. Fire Official William Behnke; inspectors Joseph Cornforth and Dennis Rosenbaum. The fee sheet is dated January 2022 (PDF metadata); no newer fee sheet found. The PDF text extraction shows '$9 0.00' for the middle tier, which is a spacing artifact of $90.00. The Bureau's web page still says it is the fire code agency for Waterford Township under a 1996 agreement, but the DCA LEA Registry (July 2026) says that shared service ended in April 2025. The DCA registry codes Berlin Borough's LEA as 'F' (fire department).
